situation: A profile named plain already exists, built from sample a alone (existing-profile.json stands in for ~/.claude/humanize-technical-prose/profiles/plain.json). The author runs `--build-profile plain ../07-profile-from-two-samples/b.md`, naming only the new sample. The stand-in stores its sample relative to this fixture; a real profile stores the resolved, absolute path, so a rebuild finds it from any directory.
git_state: not applicable: build mode edits no draft
expected_guard: the profile is rebuilt from a and b together: both are measured, both are read for slips, and the report gives 2 samples
must_not: replace the profile with one built from b alone
add b's counts to the old totals without re-measuring a
carry over a's old slip tally instead of reading a again
why_this_fixture_exists: Adding a sample is the common case once a profile exists. Overwriting would silently lose the first sample, and summing old and new totals would double-count phrases that recur across them.
